name: Kubernetes
tagline: Container orchestration with kubectl, APIs, dry-run, and declarative resources.
shortDescription: Kubernetes exposes a declarative API, kubectl CLI, dry-run, server-side apply, RBAC, events, and logs.
agentSummary: Agents can inspect clusters, propose manifests, diff/apply changes, and read logs if RBAC is scoped tightly.
bestFor: Cluster operations, deployments, rollouts, logs, events, and declarative app infrastructure.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: Cluster-wide permissions, secrets, deletes, and production rollouts need strict human review. Deploys, secret changes, IAM, billing, networking, deletes, and rollback paths have high production blast radius; require scoped credentials and review gates. CLI access is powerful but can run destructive local or production commands; prefer dry runs, preview environments, and non-production credentials. API automation needs client-side throttling, idempotency where supported, pagination limits, retries, and audit logging.
pricingSummary: Open-source; managed cluster pricing depends on cloud provider.
authModel: Kubeconfig, RBAC, service accounts, contexts, and admission policies.
accountCreation: Local clusters or managed cloud clusters; no central signup.
browserSupport: Dashboards vary; CLI is usually better for agents.

capabilities.detail: kubectl supports get, describe, logs, diff, apply, rollout, and dry-run workflows.
